rfm_tuples.R: Implied: insider transactions of board members and the founder-family principal stockholder group reflect ordinary capital management, not informational asymmetry about future earnings power.
rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for all open-market dispositions (code S) by named officers and directors in the 24 months pre-cutoff; cross-reference timing with DOJ CID, peak egg prices, and the subsequent FY26 earnings trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (EDGAR ownership.xml direct parse) + insider_vs_calendar (Form 4 dates vs 8-K calendar)
rfm_tuples.M_value: On 2025-04-17, Board Chair Adolphus B. Baker disposed 1,287,616 shares in two-line code-S transactions at $90.60 for $116.6M aggregate proceeds (split: 140,266 + 1,147,350). This was the executed leg of a registered secondary offering of 2,978,740 shares at $92.75 (gross $276.3M) by Baker plus the four Adams family daughters (Dinnette Adams Baker, Luanne Adams, Nancy Adams Briggs, Laurel Adams Krodel) underwritten by Goldman Sachs — disclosed in 8-K filed 2025-04-17 (Item 1.01). The secondary occurred (a) two days after the Class A Conversion (Apr 14, 2025) collapsed the dual-class structure that had locked in family control; (b) approximately one month AFTER the Company received the DOJ Antitrust Division Civil Investigative Demand in March 2025; (c) at the FY2025 peak earnings of $25.04 EPS and a record net average shell egg price of $3.134/dozen — i.e., the cyclical top. Subsequent Form 4 activity shows ONLY ONE meaningful open-market PURCHASE by a named officer during the entire 24-month window: Chief Strategy Officer Keira L. Lombardo bought 2,800 shares aggregating ~$259K at $92.18-92.40 on 2025-10-02, BEFORE the drawdown (CALM was still ~$92 in early Oct 2025). Through the actual Q2 (Jan 2026) and Q3 (Apr 2026) earnings declines and the deep drawdown, NO C-suite or director — including CEO Sherman Miller, CFO Max P. Bowman, COO Michael Todd Walters, Chair Adolphus Baker, or any outside director — placed any open-market code-P purchase. The Jan 2026 cluster of 13 Form 4 filings was uniformly grant/award (code A) — annual restricted-stock awards from the 2012 Omnibus Plan ($0 cost basis), not conviction buys. Other code-S sales in window: VP-Sales Hardin (Feb 2024, $295K), COO Walters (Jul 2024, $211K), GC Holladay (Aug 2024, $106K), Poole (multiple, ~$374K total). Aggregate insider open-market sell:buy dollar ratio is ~450:1 across the trailing 24 months.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the framework's textbook honesty-alpha negative signal. The structural fact pattern — founder-family principal stockholder exit, executed at the cyclical peak via underwritten secondary, one month post-DOJ-CID, accompanied by zero conviction buying from operating management through a deep subsequent drawdown — is the exact opposite of the ABG-pattern (CEO and director scaling-in during weakness). Two mitigating frames: (1) the secondary was registered, disclosed, and the Adams daughters' liquidity event was structurally inevitable post-Class-A-Conversion, so this is not 'opportunistic hidden dumping'; (2) Baker retains a continuing ~2.5M-share position. But the framework grades on signaling: even a fully disclosed, perfectly legal $276M family exit at the top, followed by no operating-management buying into a 32% drawdown, constitutes informed-insider negative-conviction evidence. Note this is NOT classified SEVERE because the disclosure was complete (S-3, 8-K, and Form 4 all filed on time).

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 3 Legal Proceedings (filed Jul 2025): "In March 2025, the Company received a Civil Investigative Demand ('CID') from the Department of Justice ('DOJ') in connection with an antitrust investigation to determine whether there is, has been or may be a violation of the antitrust laws by anticompetitive conduct by and among egg producers. The Company is complying with the CID and cooperating with the investigation. Management cannot predict the eventual scope, duration or outcome of these investigations and is unable to estimate the amount or range of potential losses, if any, at this time."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification) — given a DOJ antitrust CID against the largest U.S. shell-egg producer at the cyclical peak, verify whether the matter has expanded post-10-K (subsequent 10-Q filings) — track new state AG actions, MDL transfers, and putative class-action filings — and whether the issuer's risk-factor narrative kept pace.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q Note 10 — Legal Proceedings, filed 2026-04-01) + cross-check Q1/Q2 FY26 disclosures
rfm_tuples.M_value: Expansion is severe and was not anticipated by the 10-K's bland language. Q3 FY26 10-Q discloses: (a) AUGUST 2025 — subpoena from State of New York Attorney General re anticompetitive conduct and high egg prices; (b) MARCH 2026 — second state subpoena from State of Washington on the same subject; (c) additional state Attorneys General have either sought to join the DOJ investigation or have requested access to the Company's confidential DOJ disclosures; (d) FEBRUARY 10, 2026 — the Joint Panel on Multidistrict Litigation issued a Transfer Order consolidating private antitrust class actions (direct and indirect purchasers, Sherman Act §1 claims tied to the 2022 HPAI outbreak's pricing dynamics) and transferring them to the Western District of Wisconsin for pretrial proceedings (MDL). The 10-K (Jul 2025) disclosed only the DOJ CID; the entire state-AG cascade and the federal MDL are post-10-K developments fully visible in the Q3 FY26 10-Q. Separately, the Kraft/General Mills/Nestle (Egg Products Plaintiffs) legacy case from the 2008-era MDL No. 2002 remains active and on remand to N.D. Illinois post-Kellogg settlement.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's blanket 'cannot predict, unable to estimate' boilerplate has, in 10 months, materialized into a coordinated multi-front antitrust attack: federal DOJ + at least 2 state AGs + federal MDL of private class actions. None of this was foreseeable from the 10-K's two-sentence CID note, and the company still records no accrual. This is the dominant tail risk and was actively understated at 10-K-filing time. The framework's call here is the Mode-B catch: given the CID's existence (Mode A passes — DOJ confirmed), Mode B asks what ELSE should be verifiable, and the verifiable answer (10-Q + MDL court docket) is a much larger contingent liability profile than the 10-K conveyed.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K FY2025 MD&A: "Net sales [$4,261,885 thousand] ... Net income attributable to Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. [$1,220,048 thousand] ... Net average shell egg price (a) $3.134 ... Average UB Southeast Large Index ..." — Management's executive overview frames FY2025 as a record driven by HPAI-constrained supply and stresses cyclicality.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check FY2025 (May 31, 2025) record results against the three sequential FY2026 10-Qs to test whether the cyclical normalization is consistent with the issuer's risk framing, and whether the rate of decline has been adequately telegraphed.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Statements of Income + Q1/Q2/Q3 FY26 Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Quarterly cadence (net sales / diluted EPS / Y-o-Y change): FY2025 full year $4,261.9M / $24.95 / +338%. Q1 FY26 (Aug 2025) $922.6M / $4.12 / +35% YoY. Q2 FY26 (Nov 2025) $769.5M / $2.13 / -52% YoY. Q3 FY26 (Feb 2026) $666.9M / $1.06 / -90% YoY. Q3 gross margin collapsed from 50.5% (Q3 FY25) to 17.9% (Q3 FY26); cost of sales ramped from 49.5% of revenue to 82.1%. HPAI depopulation, the dominant supply-constraint driver of FY2025 prices, dropped 70.6% Q3-over-Q3 (13.2M hens Q3 FY26 vs 45.0M Q3 FY25); total U.S. table-egg layer flock recovered to 310.8M (+2.2% Y/Y in Q3 FY26). 39-week FY26 EPS $7.34 vs $17.92 prior — i.e., the full-year FY26 run rate is collapsing toward ~$8 from FY25's $24.95.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The cyclicality was extensively risk-flagged in the 10-K — the issuer is NOT lying; this is a commodity-price reversion, well telegraphed in the 'Industry Background' and 'Risk Factors' sections. However, the speed of reversion (Q3 EPS -90% in two quarters from peak) and the gross-margin compression to 17.9% is steeper than the 10-K's verbal warnings imply, and the company continued aggressive cash returns ($180.5M dividends + $74.9M buybacks in H1 FY26 = $255M financing outflow) into the collapse. Moderate not severe because the framework rewards transparent disclosure; CALM's reporting is fully on-time and accurate.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 7 and Note 2 — Echo Lake Foods acquired June 2, 2025 for $275.4M cash; presented as strategic diversification into prepared foods to 'reduce earnings volatility' and 'expand customer relationships.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the issuer's stated 'reduce earnings volatility' rationale, verify (a) whether more acquisitions followed at the cyclical peak; (b) whether goodwill/intangibles increased materially; (c) whether the prepared-foods segment is actually cushioning the cyclical decline in Q3 FY26.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q Notes 2 and 11; balance sheet at Feb 28, 2026)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three acquisitions in 9 months at the cyclical peak: (1) Echo Lake Foods, $275.4M, closed Jun 2, 2025 — added $40.3M goodwill and $36.8M intangibles; (2) Clean Egg, LLC, $23.7M, closed Oct 10, 2025; (3) Creighton Brothers LLC/Crystal Lake LLC, $128.5M, closed Mar 2, 2026 (subsequent event, disclosed in Q3 FY26 Note 11) — adds 3.2M layers + 865K pullets + Indiana operations. Goodwill stepped up from $46.8M (May 2025) to $87.1M (Feb 2026), and intangibles from $15.2M to $53.4M. Cumulative cash deployed in M&A in this 9-month window: ~$427.6M, all near peak prices. On the cushion test: Q3 FY26 prepared foods sales increased $51.9M Y/Y entirely due to Echo Lake, but consolidated gross profit still collapsed 83% Q-over-Q ($716M Q3 FY25 → $119M Q3 FY26) — the prepared-foods diversification did NOT meaningfully cushion the egg-cycle decline at this scale.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch on the 'reduce volatility' framing: spending $428M at the cyclical peak across three deals — including Creighton at $128.5M closed AFTER Q2 FY26 had already shown the cycle was rolling over — looks like a classic peak-of-cycle capital allocation error. The Echo Lake purchase price represented ~22.5% of FY2025 net income, but its Q3 FY26 contribution was insufficient to offset the egg-cycle reversion. No impairment recorded yet — goodwill ($87.1M) at Feb 2026 is small enough that even a 50% write-down would be only $43.5M — but the framework's signaling concern is that management's 'reduce volatility' narrative is undermined by the Q3 math.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 FY26 10-Q Note 10 (Subsequent to filing of 10-K): "On December 9, 2025, the court entered a final judgment imposing approximately $420,000 in total penalties for all defendants and awarding certain non-monetary remedies, including injunctive relief. Pursuant to the final judgment, the Company is to pay approximately $70,000 in penalties." Includes appointment of a special master, $10M initial fund within 5 days, $5M ongoing replenishment, 30-year term, jointly and severally with co-defendants.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the magnitude and time horizon of the long-tail environmental injunctive relief versus the dismissive monetary-penalty framing in the disclosure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Final judgment in State of Oklahoma v. Cal-Maine Foods et al. (Watershed Pollution Litigation, Dec 9, 2025): direct cash penalty trivial ($70K Cal-Maine portion of $420K total). But the injunctive relief — special master, court-supervised remediation plan, $10M initial joint-and-several funding within 5 days of special-master appointment plus ongoing $5M replenishment whenever fund balance falls below $5M, for 30 years — is a multi-decade contingent obligation. Company expects to appeal and 'does not currently expect to have a material share of the funding' but the verbal hedge is not quantified. No accrual recorded. This case originated in 2005 (originally Tyson, Cargill, et al.; Cal-Maine was added later) and the 2025 ruling is the culmination of a 20-year proceeding.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The disclosure frames the case by the $70K monetary penalty, which is immaterial, but the 30-year joint-and-several remediation funding obligation is materially under-quantified. Mode B catch: given the judgment exists (Mode A passes), Mode B asks what the actual financial exposure is, and the answer (multi-decade J&S fund) is materially worse than the issuer's framing implies. Not severe because there is co-defendant cost-sharing and an appeal pending.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Risk Factor: "HPAI is currently widespread in the wild bird population worldwide ... outbreaks within our facilities ... could have a material adverse effect." Q3 FY26 MD&A frames HPAI depopulations as substantially down (-70.6% Y/Y in Q3 FY26).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify whether the 'improving HPAI' narrative holds in the most recent disclosures.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q Subsequent Events) + USDA flock-depopulation context cited by issuer
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 FY26 10-Q Subsequent Events: 'On March 14, 2026, subsequent to the third quarter of fiscal 2026, we experienced an HPAI outbreak within our pullet facility in Maryland resulting in the depopulation of approximately 350,000 pullets.' First Cal-Maine HPAI hit since FY2024 (Kansas and Texas) and notably in a newly acquired (ISE) production region. Calendar 2026 industry-wide depopulations through March 30: 17.6M layer hens/pullets (already 39% of full-year 2024's 40.2M total in just three months). USDA CDC bulletin (cited by company): 1,088 dairy herds in 19 states infected, 71 human cases reported.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The improving HPAI narrative is being challenged. The Maryland pullet facility hit is small in absolute terms (350K birds is <1% of Cal-Maine's 48.3M-layer flock) but it (a) breaks the 'no Cal-Maine HPAI since 2024' implied trajectory and (b) hits a region acquired in the recent ISE deal — i.e., expansion footprint is concentrating biosecurity risk. Mode B: the company's Q3 results-day narrative (Apr 1, 2026) had to immediately retract its own quietly improving HPAI framing 17 days later when the Maryland outbreak was disclosed. Not severe because the disclosure was prompt and bird count is small.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and Q3 FY26 10-Q: 'Cal-Maine has a variable dividend policy ... pays a dividend to stockholders of its Common Stock ... in an amount equal to one-third (1/3) of such quarterly net income. ... Following a quarter for which the Company does not report net income attributable to Cal-Maine Foods, Inc., the Company will not pay a dividend for a subsequent profitable quarter until the Company is profitable on a cumulative basis computed from the date of the most recent quarter for which a dividend was paid.'
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the dividend trajectory and quantify the mechanical step-down already in motion at cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q balance sheet dividends-payable line + financing cash flows)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dividends payable line on balance sheet, sequentially: May 31, 2025 = $114.2M; Aug 30, 2025 = $66.5M; Nov 29, 2025 = $34.3M; Feb 28, 2026 = $16.8M. Sequential collapse of 85% over three quarters as quarterly net income falls. Dividends paid 39-week FY26: $180.5M cash. If Q4 FY26 net income goes negative (plausible at Q3 EPS $1.07 declining trajectory and gross margin 17.9%), the formula mechanically suspends dividends until cumulative profitability is restored. CALM is held in income/yield mandates and a dividend suspension is a known forced-seller catalyst.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The formula is fully transparent, but the mechanical-suspension trigger is not headlined in the 10-K's 'Dividends' section — it requires reading the second paragraph. At Q3 FY26 run-rate of $50.5M net income (vs $508M Y/Y), one more leg down likely triggers the suspension clause. Mode B catch: the issuer discloses the rule but does not stress-test it. Income-oriented holders are at risk of forced-selling on a Q4 print.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 FY26 10-Q: 'In February 2025, the Company announced a $500 million share repurchase program ... 11/30/25 to 12/27/25: 0 shares; 12/28/25 to 01/24/26: 354,864 shares at $73.63 avg; 01/25/26 to 02/28/26: 0 shares. 354,864 $73.63 329,830 $350,841,356.'
rfm_tuples.f: Verify execution discipline of the announced $500M buyback against the realized price path and the company's own knowledge of the cyclical-peak setup.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q Item 2 Issuer Purchases table + Q1 and Q2 FY26 equivalents) + cash-flow statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Buyback execution sequence: Feb 2025 (program announced at $500M, when stock ~$100+ and FY25 not yet closed). Q4 FY25 (Mar-May 2025) — Baker family secondary at $92.75 / $90.60 net was the dominant insider-action transaction, not buyback. Q1 FY26 (Jun-Aug 2025) — minimal buybacks; net financing $74.9M in H1 FY26 includes treasury purchases. 39-week FY26 treasury-stock purchase: $74.9M cash (per cash-flow statement). Q3 FY26 disclosed buyback: 354,864 shares at $73.63 = $26.1M in the Dec 28-Jan 24 window only. ~$351M of original $500M authorization still available. Net effect: at cutoff price (~$72 implied from -32.1% drawdown from ~$106 peak), the company has used only ~30% of authorization, and the average execution price ($73.63 in Q3 FY26 window) is lower than the secondary offering insiders captured ($92.75) — meaning family insiders cashed at the high while the corporate buyback didn't deploy at scale at the peak.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital-allocation asymmetry: insiders captured the cyclical peak via secondary, but the corporate buyback machinery did not. The buyback IS executing now into weakness (which is correct on its own merits) but the size has been small relative to the $1.22B FY25 net income and the $500M authorization. Mode B: the framework reads this as 'insiders prioritized personal liquidity at the top over corporate buyback at the top' — a governance/alignment concern. Not severe because both actions were disclosed.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Risk Factors and Business sections: extensive disclosure of state cage-free mandates and the capex required to convert conventional layer capacity. 10-K notes Company has 'continued conversion to cage-free' and is making investments.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the capex and the cyclical reversion, verify the financial-flexibility position (debt, cash) at cutoff to determine whether mandated conversion + acquisition spend is straining the balance sheet.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q3 FY26 10-Q balance sheet + Note on debt) + 10-K Item 7A liquidity discussion
rfm_tuples.M_value: Balance-sheet snapshot Feb 28, 2026: cash & equivalents + investments ~$700M+ (down from $812M at May 31, 2025); property/plant/equipment net $1,221M (up from $1,027M reflecting capex + acquisitions); total assets $3,139M; total liabilities $432M; stockholders' equity $2,704M; retained earnings $2,801M. Credit facility (Amended Nov 2021): $250M senior secured revolver, $0 borrowed, $4.7M LCs outstanding. Two financial covenants: Total Funded Debt to Capitalization ≤50% (deeply compliant at near-zero leverage); Min Tangible Net Worth $700M + 50% of cumulative net income — CALM is far above this floor. In compliance per 10-K certification at May 31, 2025 and Q3 FY26.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Despite the cyclical collapse and the $428M acquisition spend, the balance sheet is fortress-grade: $700M+ liquidity, $0 revolver drawn, equity $2.7B, no debt of material consequence, full covenant compliance with massive cushions. This is the offsetting positive signal — CALM can weather a multi-quarter cycle trough and absorb antitrust litigation outcomes without solvency stress. The drawdown is earnings-and-multiple compression on a healthy balance sheet, not distress.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1: 'Our top three customers accounted for an aggregate of 49.2%, 49.0%, and 50.1% of our net sales dollars for fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. Our largest customer, Walmart Inc. (including Sam's Club), accounted for 33.6%, 34.0%, and 34.2% of net sales dollars for fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.'
rfm_tuples.f: Verify concentration trend stability and Mode B — given the antitrust scrutiny on egg pricing, assess whether Walmart's pricing power against Cal-Maine has materially shifted.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K customer-concentration disclosure) + Q3 FY26 net sales / gross margin compression as proxy for pricing power
rfm_tuples.M_value: Walmart concentration stable at ~34% over three years. Q3 FY26 net average shell egg price collapsed (cost of sales 82.1% of revenue vs 49.5% prior year) — most of the volatility is industry-wide pricing reversion, not Walmart-specific renegotiation. No disclosure of customer loss or material contract repricing. However, the framework notes that DOJ antitrust scrutiny + state AG subpoenas focused on the 2022-2025 high-price era inherently invite the largest customers (Walmart) to push for retroactive concessions or to demand structural pricing reform — which is a Mode-B verifiable risk via subsequent contract amendments, but not yet observable in filings pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Customer concentration disclosure is honest and well-quantified. The Mode-B link — antitrust scrutiny → customer leverage shift — is hypothetical at cutoff (no disclosed evidence of Walmart renegotiation), so the framework grades this UNVERIFIABLE rather than MODERATE. Note for future cycles: the next 10-K customer-concentration table is the verifier.

summary: CALM is a Mode-B-rich case. Mode A passes: every disclosure (DOJ CID, secondary offering, acquisitions, HPAI events, cyclical decline) is on time and accurate. Mode B finds three substantive gaps: (1) the 10-K's two-sentence DOJ-CID treatment has expanded over 10 months into NY+WA AG subpoenas, JPML MDL consolidation, and additional state-AG participation — none accrued; (2) Form 4 evidence shows a $276M family secondary at the cyclical peak (one month post-CID), followed by ZERO open-market buying by C-suite or directors through the entire 32% drawdown — only a $259K CSO buy pre-drawdown; (3) the variable-dividend formula is at the edge of mechanical suspension. Offsetting: balance sheet is fortress-grade ($700M+ liquidity, $0 debt). VERDICT: SHORT-tier — multi-front antitrust expansion is the dominant under-disclosed tail risk, insider Form-4 evidence is the strongest negative signal under the framework (informed-insider exit at peak + no operating-management conviction buying into 32% drawdown), and earnings are still rolling over (Q3 EPS -90% Y/Y, gross margin halved); valuation is supported only by the fortress balance sheet.
